gaps.note: The paper has m=h^3=1000000 (line 656), which is greater than 2^19=524288, so mu<2^19 is false. The paper (line 1332) states m<2^20 (with log 2<1, so log m<20). The conclusion ln mu<20 still holds, but the stated premise is wrong; correct is mu<2^20.

gaps.quote: a forward invocation from $X$ to $Y$ subtracts $x_S$ from $y_S$ and changes no other value (cited)
gaps.note: The paper's Lemma (lines 729-730) says a forward invocation changes y_S to y_S+x_S, i.e. it adds x_S to y_S; the inverse schedule is the one that subtracts. Subtracting also contradicts the page's next sentence, since the shear H<-H+D adds D to H.

gaps.quote: The outer two take linear time.
gaps.note: The page does not say why D<-D-H and D<-H-D cost only linear time. The reason (paper Section on tape interchange) is that they update the later field using the earlier field in tape order, which a single scan can do; the reader is not given this and cannot check it.
